$comment: The M1 item catalog, per design-bible §5. Volumes are cubic metres; cargo capacity is volumetric rather than slot-based, which is what makes bulk hauling a real profession.

items.name: Scrap Alloy
items.$comment: Hand-gatherable with no tool, so a brand-new character always has somewhere to start. Common to every world, and the one raw material that is: Joe, 9 October 2026 (task 184). Every homeworld has it beside its outpost.
items.$priceComment: Whole credits per unit, like quest rewards. This is the floor that guarantees nobody is ever stuck: at zero credits a player can neither start a job nor place a sell order, since both charge up front, so ore would be unsellable exactly when it is all they own. Priced to be the worst option available -- selling to another player must always beat it, or the player market never forms. One credit against a 15 cr job fee means a few minutes of gathering unsticks you and nothing more.

items.$starterComment: The four starter ores, one per homeworld and planet-locked to it (ADR-0008; Joe, 9 October 2026, task 184). Mechanically identical -- volume, price, deposit size, respawn, tool and level -- so no race's first hour is easier than another's (design-bible section 4), and materially distinct, so each world's ore is hauled rather than found everywhere. A new player is still never waiting on a market: their own world has their ore and the scrap beside it. Not the level-15 materials below, which feed the cross-faction tier. All four are the family starter_ore, which is what quest 3 asks for, so any homeworld's ore counts toward it (task 186).
items.name: Ferrite Ore
items.$comment: Terra's. Tool-gated behind crude_mining_laser. Terra keeps the familiar metal because it is the familiar world (design-bible section 4). Found on the Capital as well until 9 October 2026, when it became Terra's alone.
items.$priceComment: Twice scrap because it is tool-gated and slower to gather, but still a floor rather than a valuation. Twenty ore refines into four plates; if four plates ever sell for less than the 40 cr this pays, the floor has been set too high and the refining chain is pointless.

items.name: Oxide Salt
items.$comment: Ares'. Rust-red salt crust from a dry world, cut out of the desert floor. Tool-gated behind crude_mining_laser, and ferrite's equal in everything but where it is found.

items.name: Rootstone
items.$comment: Verdance's. Stone the living planet has grown roots through. Not 'heartwood_amber' as design-bible section 4 first proposed, which would have been a second amber on a world that already has Luminous Amber. Tool-gated behind crude_mining_laser, and ferrite's equal in everything but where it is found.

items.name: Blackiron Ore
items.$comment: Grimhold's. Heavy dark iron from a heavy dark world. Not 'blackslag' as design-bible section 4 first proposed, which would have been a second slag on a world that already has Grimhold Slag. Tool-gated behind crude_mining_laser, and ferrite's equal in everything but where it is found.

items.name: Structural Plate
items.$comment: Denser than its inputs by design: refining should make hauling easier, not harder.
items.$nameComment: Structural Plate since 9 October 2026 (Joe; task 185), because it is refined from every homeworld's ore and plate made from oxide salt is not ferrite. The key keeps the old name: renaming a content key orphans every stack, order and recipe that holds it, and the seeder never removes the old row (task 188).

items.$lockedComment: The four level-15 planet-locked raw materials (ADR-0008), which the cross-faction frame consumes. Each occurs on exactly one homeworld and nowhere else, which is what makes hauling a profession and gives the faction line something to be a line between. Until 9 October 2026 the starter chain above was deliberately unlocked, scrap and ferrite everywhere; since task 184 only scrap is common, and each world's starter ore is locked to it, beside the scrap a new player needs.
items.name: Terran Ferrite
items.$comment: Terra. Ocean-quenched iron from a temperate world -- the mundane one, and the baseline the other three are strange against.

items.name: Ferric Regolith
items.$comment: Ares. Red desert dust, bulky for its worth, so hauling it is a decision rather than a reflex.

items.name: Luminous Amber
items.$comment: Verdance. Resin from a planet that reads as alive -- dense in value and small in volume, so it is what a fast ship carries and a slow one gets caught with.

items.name: Grimhold Slag
items.$comment: Grimhold. Named in ADR-0008 as the example of a material that exists in one place and nowhere else.

items.name: Composite Frame
items.$comment: The first thing that cannot be built by one race alone: it consumes all four planet-locked materials, so two of them must cross the faction line to reach any given builder. ADR-0008 calls this the load-bearing decision of the whole document -- without a recipe like this the global market has nothing to trade across and the PvP split is scenery.

items.name: Crude Thruster
items.$comment: Was the one intentional exception to everything being player-made, bought from a faction supply order that was never built -- so the questline could not be finished at all from the first day of content until 6 September (task 148). craft_crude_thruster makes it now, under electronics, brought forward one milestone. Joe on being offered the shop instead: every item in the game should be craftable.

items.name: Freighter
items.$comment: The second ship tier, and the only thing that consumes a composite frame. Without a consumer the frame was a dead end: EconSim ran five years and found builders made about twenty, could not sell them, and stopped -- taking with them the only reason ore ever crosses the faction line. A frame that nothing needs makes ADR-0008's contested zone scenery, which is the exact failure that document calls load-bearing. This is what gives the frame standing demand, and it is deliberately a hauler: the ship you want once you are trading across factions is the one that carries more.

items.name: Laser Rifle
items.$comment: The first weapon, tier 1 (task 194). A bolt of 55 every half second is 110 damage a second, so 1,000 health falls in about 9 s of hits on the body from the front: ADR-0017's 8-12 s fight. 150 m is a guess at a rifle's reach on a 20 km world; the drafts' basic attack is a semi-automatic bolt (weapons/laser-rifle.md). Heat, the focused beam and the trees come later.
